column1: # The function-quality audit ledger — coverage AND open findings, one row per .c file
# in src/. No exceptions: tools/guardrails.sh checks this list against the tree in both
# directions, so a file can never be silently skipped — a new .c file has to be
# classified here before `make guardrails` passes again.
# THE STANDARD — four questions per function, asked when a file is audited:
#   1. Does it name one real domain concept? (Not "these lines appeared together twice.")
#   2. Is its signature minimal and honest? No dead parameters — a signature that names
#      a parameter it never reads over-claims its edges, the mirror of a missing const.
#      Broad-and-const is fine; broad-and-mutable is not. The write set drives the count.
#   3. Is claimed purity real? For anything under a *_pure/ directory: no static mutable
#      state, no I/O, no RNG, no clock, every pointer const. The directory name is a
#   4. Is the duplication genuine? Extract only where a real, nameable concept exists —
#      if merging two similar blocks needs a mode flag to keep them apart, they were two
#      rules that happened to look alike, and merging makes the code less tractable.
#   audited   read against the four questions above
#   open      not audited yet, and nothing blocks auditing it
#   deferred  a scheduled slice rewrites or deletes the file, so auditing it now is
#             churn — the audit is part of THAT slice's exit criteria instead
# THE NOTE COLUMN carries open findings — things a read turned up that were not fixed
# on the spot, marked "OPEN FINDING:". They live here rather than in prose so they sit
# next to the file they are about and cannot drift away from the tree. A finding that
# gets fixed leaves this file; what it taught goes to the docs' history instead.

purity verified — three total functions of their arguments, no state, no branch on anything but the arguments' own ranges. Written and audited in the same commit, which is the only honest moment: a file whose whole content is one derivation is read completely by whoever derived it, and reading it again later proves less. The clamps are the only conditionals and each has a named reason at its use site (a sweep of zero frames would be an unrepresentable state; a power outside [0,1] must clamp rather than invert the meter).

ACTUALIZE, split from execute_actions.c at the stage split (2026-11-05) and audited there: one stage function in the engine's own order, two actualizers it alone calls, all four questions answered yes. Fixed on the spot: the free-walk answer emitted its event from both branches of a test that did not decide it, and two comments named a flag and a function that do not exist.

audited on arrival: the AI half of the CONTROL stage — one dispatcher that hands each AI team only its own channel, and the controller's one init. The World arrives const, so what a controller may touch is the signature

audited at the controller-eviction slice, which rewrote it: one function per beat of the dance (batter choice, pre-pitch arming, recall, the flight, the power commit, the loose-hit advance) where there was one ~225-line function; the strategy is derived from the const World each time it is asked rather than remembered; the per-pitch plan is one struct with one clear. Two RNG draws that were arguments to one call (unspecified order in C) are now two statements, in the order gcc had been using OPEN FINDING (2026-10-27): arm_runners_for_the_pitch reads runner_commitments.armed — the engine's record of its own RUN_FORWARD — to stay self-limiting. Not counted by the read-back ratchet and arguably durable world state (the engine fires it at the release), but it is the shape the fourth law watches for; the next audit of this file should decide and say.

audited at the controller-eviction slice: three dead includes and an unused macro removed, throw_ball_to_base made file-local, the World taken const. update_catching_ai is long but one concept — the fielding controller's two situations (nobody has the ball / somebody does) — and the drop-or-throw branch reads as one decision, so it is left whole OPEN FINDING: the controller declares a throw home from the pitcher's own hands on every frame he holds the ball with no lead runner — refused at the gate as RULE_THROW_TARGET_TOO_CLOSE, 6,262 times over 42 golden runs (2026-10-11). Harmless, and the gate is right to refuse it, but a controller asking for something it can see is impossible is a small strategy defect.

split from game_manipulation.c at the stage split (2026-11-05) and audited there: one function, a fielder meets the loose ball, detected and enacted at once. OPEN FINDING (2026-10-27): a batted ball still names the PITCHER as released_by — a hit does not set it — so the pitcher cannot catch a batted fly before it bounces, and neither can any fielder within PLAYER_TOO_CLOSE_TO_CATCH_LIMIT (15) of him; the guard was written for the pitcher's own pitch and for a thrower's own throw. MEASURED in the audit the same day, over the 42 golden runs: of the frames in which a fielder was within catching reach of a batted ball that had not touched the ground, the guard refused 93 of 141 in AI-vs-AI play (70 the pitcher himself, 23 fielders near him) and 155 of 157 in the human-batting runs. In pesäpallo the lukkari is an ulkopelaaja like any other and his catch is a koppi, so this is a mechanics defect. The guard is probably load-bearing, though — at contact the ball passes right by the pitcher — so the fix is a design (who may meet a batted ball, and from when), not deleting the check: its own slice, measured against the fielding bands, and felt.

OPEN FINDING: calculate_free_walk prints "[CRITICAL LOGIC ERROR] Ghost Runner" — a batting player on BASE_HOME who is not the active batter — and carries on; reached in fuzzed human-vs-human play (golden runs h2h1, h2h4, h2h7, 2026-10-11), never in AI play or the test tiers. Unexplained, and a printf that says CRITICAL and continues is not a check: find the state, then make it unrepresentable or assert it.

OPEN FINDING (2026-10-27): reset_for_foul_play clears the at-bat with the rest of the play, so a batter restored to the plate after a foul has lost §32's right to leave home until the next release — the right is the turn's, granted at its first pitch. Rules question, not a refactor: discuss before changing. The reset building blocks joined it from common_logic.c (2026-11-05). Rename to something like is_runner_burnt_in_base_race, with the whole terminology pass

OPEN FINDING (2026-11-05 audit): §32 — the batter may leave home once the turn's first pitch has left the lukkari's hand — is asked inside run_to_next_base, not at the gate: a RUN_COMMIT the gate let through is silently dropped there, a permission with no RuleId, against the claim that every permission is the gate's. It also guards the engine's own commits (the release, the hit), where it can never refuse, so moving it is the rules project's: a RuleId at the gate for the batter's commit, and the mechanic's check kept as an invariant or deleted.
